pitfalls.title: strategic_scope_effective_models_and_execution_evidence
symptoms: Pure forward SAA is blocked by product-only navigation, or missing products erase strategic budgets.
Model output is displayed while funding or TAA consumes old manual moments.
Changing execution frequency changes cost basis or hides actual holding-budget breaches.
trigger_actions: change mandates, strategic universes, implementation maps or CMA generation
change SAA policy consumption, TAA signals, clocks or product handoff
check_before_edit: Preserve product-first workflows. Independent strategic definitions may support CMA/SAA without NAV; missing maps remain explicit and block product implementation, not class-level TAA research. Confirmed strategic SAA uses frozen research proxies with real source availability; missing proxies block calculation with asset names. Never infer trading products from research proxies. Completing a map creates new versions, never rewrites old policies. SAA scope, comparison, confirmation and saved-policy screens must not require real products or surface downstream implementation blockers as SAA research problems. Preserve explicit historical mapping references and backend product-application gates; verify no-products comparison/save and TAA continuation.

Consume frozen effective moments through cma_application in search, funding and policy risk. Preserve raw model identity and hashes; posterior mean uncertainty is not asset-return risk. Never refit historical artifacts.

LTCMA V2 does not require mandate or product implementation mapping. Select the mapping at SAA policy creation without changing CMA evidence; old mapping-bound records retain their original contract. Retirement blocks new SAA/prior use while historical versions remain readable. NIW publication must recheck prior eligibility and save under the retirement governance lock; completed idempotent replay remains historical. Switching the editor to continuation clears recenter strengths and reuse consent. The SAA CMA deep link initializes once and must not override subsequent user selection or clearing during pending reads.

LTCMA has no generic forecast-horizon label: ordinary annual moments do not depend on it. Strip retired horizon_years from old requests and copied drafts, never rewrite frozen artifacts or gate NIW/SAA use by that field. Conditional scenario horizon_days is a separate real numerical input: it determines Markov transitions, period occupancy, compounded-return moments and compute budgets; preserve it and reject unsupported work explicitly. Mandate horizon_years still controls funding months and budgets. Verify old read/copy, no-horizon statistical publication, conditional horizon sensitivity and unchanged annual-model behavior.

Historical LTCMA needs an SSE calendar covering the requested end, including closed dates. A stale calendar and equally truncated NAV must not silently shorten the sample. Switching a statistical draft from strategic proxies to a product allocation clears proxy_inputs. State occupancy, applied probabilities, unestimated states and NIW asset-risk versus mean-uncertainty evidence remain distinct.

Cash-purpose floors consume frozen liquid liquidity-role assets. For typed strategic scope inputs, derive this classification from research_proxy.asset_type at the backend boundary: cash is liquid liquidity-role, market cannot retain a cash role. The UI exposes only asset type; preserve pre-existing non-cash liquidity restrictions and untyped historical contracts. Institutional manual evidence retains every topic, date and reason; researcher records are not independent approval.

Preserve original four-candidate and daily-target outputs. Risk budgets compare signed Euler shares over finite candidates; zero variance is unavailable. New kernels require actual invocation, fixed signatures and PID-bound warmup.

Box mean uncertainty and the opt-in single-CMA ellipsoid are distinct models. Preserve default box request echoes and frozen history; never substitute return covariance for missing mean covariance. Gaussian, NIW-t and finite-sample Hotelling radii have different calibrations. Nonzero variance coordinates, not numerical rank thresholds, determine the implemented dimension; singular or shrunk sample plug-in coverage needs explicit approximation consent. Multi-CMA mean-error dependence is not inferred. BL basket views reuse the original Gaussian update; diagnostics must not change asset risk or declared half-widths. State ML denominators preserve the total-moment identity, transition diagnostics do not create a multi-year forecast, and moment-proxy funding does not preserve native scenario tails.
Separate observation, decision and execution clocks. Preserve drift, lag, explicit cost basis, actual-path budget diagnostics and training-only selection. Fixed-target stress is not strategy replay.
Every positive-weight signal component must be known, complete and unexpired, without missing-component renormalization. External value/carry/macro labels do not license fabricating scores from NAV.

Use actual dated holdings for thresholds and recheck current holdings at the shared product bridge. Policy/mapping expiry needs explicit reasons. Navigation references are not current eligibility proofs. Scope-page continuation must lead to LTCMA, not directly to SAA. New-research SAA journey navigation requires a confirmed LTCMA reference; an existing policy remains returnable because it already freezes its assumptions.

Composite recommendation expiry uses each positive component age/expiry at the adopted lag-mature decision, capped by research and policy review dates; never reuse the old momentum/regime global age or a pending signal expiry.

Restoring a TAA baseline or saved decision atomically restores its frozen mandate, strategic universe and mapping references, explicitly clearing absent references. Immutable mapping reads are independent of PIT initialization; clock changes invalidate computations, not saved history.

Saved scope viewing, editing, copying and new research require distinct editor identities. Editing saves an immutable replacement; deletion retires the active entry while preserving historical IDs and hashes. Active names share a trim/casefold namespace across product and strategic stores under one lock, using the configured storage roots and rejecting corrupt peer reads. Exclude only the edited record from uniqueness checks; legacy duplicates still require renaming. Every successful save writes its new ID to the URL and clears draft/source parameters; do not use a stored journey to open an editor implicitly. Delayed deletion must inspect the latest URL and journey so it cannot clear a newer selection. Switching identity invalidates pending reads and saves; React StrictMode cleanup must not prevent the next history read. New asset IDs stay unchanged when labels or the common currency change. Descriptive annotations may be empty; actual references and quantitative gates remain required. Strategic research proxies and cash-return defaults must survive scope save/read/copy and initialize LTCMA inputs; they support class-level TAA after SAA confirmation and data checks, but never create an implementation mapping or authorize product application. Preserve cash-role/liquidity checks, adjusted-product fields, explicit weights and preview-hash invalidation. Strategic scope uses one visible save action that awaits preview and confirms with the same draft and fresh hash; check cancellation between both calls so stale validation cannot trigger a write. Show blocking reasons and request errors next to save, retain the draft after failure, and allow retry. Translate structured scope validation errors using asset names and form labels. extra_forbidden for research_proxy is a frontend/backend contract mismatch, not user input error; never drop proxy fields to make an old backend accept the request. Check the owning checkout, frontend proxy target and live OpenAPI before reloading only the affected service; source support does not prove a running process has loaded the new contract. Missing proxies are a valid scope but not complete historical evidence. Batch reference selection persists across filters/pages, applies atomically and never normalizes existing weights.
Changing an external signal kind resets both its visible JSON and submitted observations; preserve incomplete JSON while typing and block calculation until it is valid.

For parameter-average SAA, validate every source hash, V2 semantic basis, economic/proxy identity and retirement state. E2 uses the shared mixture kernel within covariance, never its total covariance or squared model weights. Preserve the fused policy marker and complete frozen multi_cma evidence; missing evidence must not fall back to legacy manual assumptions. Cross-model failures remain visible diagnostics, not an implicit all-model gate. Bound total funding work and final metadata before writing so an accepted policy remains readable.

Compatible-all-model policies require every frozen source to pass; display-only average moments cannot authorize adoption or TAA. Preserve the mode, compatibility gate and source hashes together. Solver timeout, iteration exhaustion and unresolved Phase I are not infeasibility. The compiled outer state machine owns iteration state, cut accumulation, objective bounds and numerical stopping; Python only schedules wall-clock checks between masters. Warm and audit this state machine itself, not only its LP substeps. A positive normalized Phase-I objective lower bound may certify a conflict; zero relaxed objective still requires original risk checks. Funding failure applies only to the generated common candidate, not the full feasible set; confirm using an independent stream for each model. Numeric execution audits must include the shared frontend backend/nopython/object_mode fields as well as PID-bound warmup.

Persist exact mandate_id and mandate_hash on both saved scope types. Scope details, catalog and library actions restore that binding before showing the goal or enabling save; editing inherits it and rejects replacement with another mandate. The URL selects the saved scope; its persisted association overrides a conflicting mandate parameter. A legacy association may be filled once from an explicitly chosen mandate under the shared governance lock, separately from immutable scope bytes. Never infer the historical association from allocationJourney, even if its scope ID matches: viewing another scope can retain an unrelated goal in that bookmark. Verify reopening without mandate parameters or browser storage, edit/refresh, and unchanged historical hashes.

CMA center handoff carries every explicitly selected version via repeated cma query parameters and a CMA-set-specific SAA draft. A primary ltcmaId is not a multi-model study: preserve ltcmaIds in journey links, clear them on upstream changes, and require an explicit multi-CMA mode and weights. Resolve the mandate from the persisted scope binding, never from the previous browser journey. A missing optional field must not invalidate existing single-CMA drafts. Verify this in LtcmaHandoff, MultiCmaWorkspace and allocationJourney tests. Current catalogs exclude superseded strategic scopes, but saved CMA references remain immutable and readable. On center handoff and SAA refresh, getStrategicCatalog must fetch the explicitly referenced missing scope by exact ID, restore its bound mandate and asset constraints, and never substitute a same-named active scope. Check the scope hash against frozen CMA lineage before handoff; preserve backend source and retirement gates. The scope-replacement regression in LtcmaHandoff and the ltcma browser test covers single and multiple CMA continuation.

Scenario CMA reuses exact historical run/publication/content hashes and calibrated causal recognition bound to that same reference. Recheck snapshot hashes and data/label information cutoffs against PIT. Historical and long-term scenarios accept any classification frequency and archive date: project only closed observed same-state intervals onto daily return-end dates, leave transition gaps and tails unknown, and never truncate a future-fitted run to simulate PIT. Publication identity remains exact. Conditional current probabilities still require daily causal recognition, calibrated availability/expiry, matching return dates and qualified positive-probability states. LTCMA must read the validated immutable realtime snapshot and attach calibration directly; resolve_taa_run and realtime formal-publication records belong only to TAA admission. A saved or research-display-only run with valid evidence can support conditional research; missing calibration stays unavailable with its own reason. Preserve exact historical publication binding and the unchanged TAA formal gate; test options, conditional save and TAA rejection against the same unpublished fixture. Keep every publication reference selectable for the same run/hash: retaining only the first hides realtime studies bound to a later publication. Options expose unavailable reasons on hover, keyboard focus and touch without selecting unavailable entries. Historical references require explicit user selection even when only one is eligible; preserve the dropdown and the retrospective-identification center action for empty, filtered and selected states. Restore saved bindings without choosing a new study on options refresh. The current conditional UI still auto-binds a sole eligible real-time run after matching the exact historical publication; review that behavior separately against user-selection requirements rather than generalizing it to historical evidence. Unknown state observations break transitions rather than becoming neutral states or connecting nonadjacent dates. Do not relax the existing reliability.cma_evidence restriction.

Current-state recognition probabilities, retrospective transition diagnostics and independently validated future-state forecasts are different evidence. The conditional Markov model computes research projections, period-average occupancy and compounded moments without claiming future validation. Its method is research-only: server-side SAA, NIW-prior and multi-CMA guards must reject it even if copied metadata sets downstream_eligible=true or omits validation fields. Frozen history remains readable; mutable UI state and audit flags cannot authorize downstream use.

Long-term scenario return covariance describes asset risk; block-bootstrap mean_estimation_covariance and declared marginal half-widths describe mean-estimation error. Keep both frozen and distinct, allow the existing default box uncertainty, and do not infer an ellipsoid radius from the new covariance without model-specific calibration. Seeds depend on numerical evidence and immutable references, not human notes. Readonly fixed-signature kernels must be warmed before requests; admit finite-horizon analytical work and account for all simulation batches without silently shortening the requested horizon.

Separate saved scope identity from economic compatibility. Identical ordered assets, currencies, roles, liquidity and research proxy facts may reuse CMA across scope record IDs; names, notes and saved timestamps are not economic facts. Compare actual fitted proxies separately and preserve date, return/fee/FX, retirement and research-only gates. Unchanged strategic-scope edits return the original record under the governance lock. Read derived facts from frozen snapshots without rewriting history; validate each original source hash independently in multi-CMA handoff. Scope equality does not rebind implementation mappings or choose another mandate. Wait for the initial PIT state before requesting LTCMA options; do not temporarily request today and strand initialization when a historical cutoff loads later. Configuration compatibility does not remove the existing NIW positive-definite-prior requirement; fixed zero-risk cash remains a separate numerical limitation.

SAA frontier diagnostics must remain independent of candidate feasibility: overlay the absolute return floor and risk cap rather than filtering away the curve. Use frozen effective moments and the same weight/cash/liquidity boundaries; show each original model separately in common mode. Failed grid points are gaps, not zeros or proof of infeasibility. Disable policy comparison only after a verified return upper bound or the warmed continuous solver certifies target infeasibility; discrete grid misses and exhausted budgets are not proof. Common mode must test one weight vector across all original models. Keep benchmark and funding gates separate, invalidate both graph and comparison state immediately on input or PIT changes, and show an adjacent human-readable reason; unresolved checks retain candidate comparison. SAA interaction tests must mock policy/frontier with typed execution and target evidence, await the enabled comparison button, and verify the chart loaded so API-error fallback cannot produce a false pass. Finding the button only proves it exists while the debounced frontier request may still be pending. Mock only the chart renderer in jsdom, not the frontier gate; LtcmaHandoff also covers pending and certified-infeasible responses preventing policy/preview requests.

Step-02 scope screening reuses historical evidence and continuous SAA solvers; never infer infeasibility from missing grid intersections. Require a verified candidate or certified bound, respect the earliest mandate/risk-reference expiry, resolve products by their explicit market code while retaining product_id identity, and leave unclassified cash/liquidity requirements undetermined. Preview product selections must reuse save assembly without writing records. Invalidate charts and conclusions immediately on scope, goal, window or PIT changes; screening does not publish LTCMA or certify funding success. A funding-pending overall verdict must not hide a verified target_check verdict: show the passed historical risk/weight check separately from unvalidated funding-path success. Echo step-01 cashflow_required_return with its solver status and compound-return basis; do not plot it as an arithmetic-return target or replace target_check with a frontier-presence heuristic. Funding comparison may project all three curves to median-path annual compound growth using the existing daily-moment adapter, retaining raw arithmetic evidence. Never compare a compound hurdle directly against arithmetic returns or double-charge fees. Only validated current-scope points can pass the hurdle screen; reference curves and finite-grid misses cannot establish feasibility or infeasibility. Keep the full funding-probability gate separate from this display verdict.

LTCMA edit and copy have different lifecycle contracts: PATCH keeps one current study entry via supersedes_cma_id and stable study_id; POST copy creates an independent study. Preserve immutable old IDs/hashes and existing SAA/TAA/NIW references, exclude only the edited record from name conflicts, and retain editing_ref in saved drafts. Recheck stale edits and deletes under the governance lock, preserve exact idempotent retry/recovery, and never resurrect a predecessor after retiring its replacement. NIW study-options must restore an explicitly selected historical prior without listing every superseded result as a new study. Verify test_ltcma_lifecycle, LtcmaCenter and the center-row browser flow.

SAA common-model frontiers overlay each frozen source. Plot a common candidate only from complete ID/hash-matched cross_model_results, including failed candidates; never plot its worst-per-metric summary as one distribution. Fusion plots the solved frontier of averaged moments, never averaged curves. Reference visibility and model legend switches must not change requests, constraints or conclusions.
SAA 方案列表只从冻结政策读取目标、范围和所有 CMA 来源，不能改用当前目录补齐同名记录或把无 policy 的回测基线列为已采纳方案；新建入口使用独立 URL token 隔离草稿。

At a full-rank LP active vertex, the face direction is exactly zero. Nearly parallel variance cuts can amplify saddle-KKT roundoff beyond the stopping tolerance and falsely report numerical_failure before the common solve. Solve the active transpose for multipliers and release a violating face instead; do not relax risk or substitute averaged moments. Regress frozen four-asset cash models against independent QCQP anchors and joint objectives in test_multi_cma_compatibility.py.

TAA research proxies align price endpoints on common observations and retain every full interval return. Market calendar differences must not fail the whole research or delete intervening P&L. Actual interval years drive cash compounding, risk, TE and utility in training, holdout, walk-forward and historical scenarios; never derive training annualization from holdout dates. Date-only proxy signals wait until after publication day, while label maturity retains the original publication date. Without complete per-market calendars, report unobserved dates as unverified closures or gaps, not confirmed missing data. Preserve frozen histories and product-only equal-period contracts; tests cover test_tactical_research_proxies.py and test_tactical_allocation_numeric.py.

Normalize requirements through return_targets: preserve arithmetic versus annual-compound basis, invert the declared moment adapter at actual portfolio volatility, and never double-charge fees. Relative explicit-numeric goals require a complete benchmark; calculate benchmark return per frozen model. Check compound requirements in reference search, SAA and fixed-weight TAA gates; preserve capital-adjustment diagnostics and separate funding probability. Historical missing basis remains arithmetic. A relaxed common-model solve followed by a failed compound candidate is not an infeasibility proof. A separate unresolved solver must not hide a numerically verified single-model frontier weight that passes all applicable return/risk bounds; failed points, unchecked benchmarks and per-model different weights cannot establish feasibility.

Copying a product research scope must carry excluded_product_keys into its independent draft and next save, just as editing does. Restoring only pool version IDs silently reintroduces excluded products.
safe_observation_methods: npm run test --prefix frontend -- --run LtcmaScenarioFields.test.tsx LtcmaScenarioSelect.test.tsx LtcmaStatisticsFields.test.tsx LtcmaCenter.test.tsx LtcmaHandoff.test.tsx

Run backend/tests/test_saa_policy_catalog.py and frontend SaaCenter / StrategicAllocationWorkspace tests; e2e/saa-center.spec.ts covers saved links, fresh draft isolation, retries and 320/768/1440px layouts.

pitfalls.title: published_sensitivity_and_scenario_boundaries
symptoms: A scenario label or hardcoded beta is presented as a calibrated macro model.
Opening a product page fits a model or reads complete training panels.
A model/cashflow/scenario preview creates files before the user confirms publication.
A product or portfolio stress calculation is persisted even though the workflow has no confirm-publish action.
A past-data model becomes fresh merely by changing as_of to today.
A negative shock is converted to a positive number while typing, or blank input becomes zero.
Missing held assets disappear from portfolio P&L or new holdings are applied to an old result.
trigger_actions: edit risk-model or scenario-transmission research
change preview, publication, artifact persistence or published-scenario application
connect business pages to published exposure artifacts
check_before_edit: Keep statistical holdout validation distinct from identified causality or certified historical PIT. Event names never supply numerical coefficients.

Unconfirmed model, cashflow, transmission and scenario previews are pure calculations: they must not call ArtifactRepository.save, create directories/locks, or persist frozen arrays. Only an explicit confirm-publish request may write research artifacts, after server-side recomputation/compilation matches the preview hash.

Product and portfolio stress impacts are transient because that workflow has no confirm-publish action. Do not reintroduce impact caching/persistence or a normal saved-impact history without an explicit product decision and publication workflow; old persisted impact IDs are read-only compatibility only.

Freeze definitions, input contracts, training outputs and publication times only on confirmed publication. Expiry uses actual joint-sample data_as_of; requested as_of does not refresh stale data. Collinear failed fits still have readable counts and blockers.

Match variable ID, contract hash and frequency; risk-return percent display, bp, percentage-point and point changes are not interchangeable. Every path row is a period change, not an accumulated level.

Use published coefficients or fixed-cashflow repricing, never manually editable betas or automatic training on consumption. Runtime reads only required mmap arrays; publication verifies complete artifacts. Cashflow repricing requires the parallel-yield semantic contract: a bp unit alone never licenses treating Shibor or policy rates as bond yield. Calendar coverage includes known closed days and is required only through the last complete analysis period.

Use stored end holdings derived from last beginning weights and last returns. Reject every missing nonzero exposure, preserve buy-and-hold versus explicit zero-cost constant weighting, and reconcile contributions to terminal wealth. Portfolio comparisons pin the same scenario, exposure release, date, notional and holding policy; show both holdings dates and do not show a partial comparison when either request fails.
Require explicit unchanged-other-factors consent. Deterministic conditional paths do not supply probabilities, VaR or ES.
Keep pinned missing/retired/expired releases visible as unavailable; never silently replace them. Reject stale drafts and ignore late requests from another product.
Retain incomplete signed input until it becomes a valid number; test negative, fractional, empty and external reset cases. Bound form containers so wide tables do not widen a mobile page.

Guard the managed data disk before confirmed publication reads/writes; no mkdir fallback on offline storage. Historical immutable published results remain readable after retirement without recalculation. Explicit source-data import remains a persisted data operation and is not treated as an unconfirmed research preview.
safe_observation_methods: npm run test --prefix frontend -- --run PublishedRiskFlow.test.tsx ResearchUI.test.tsx riskModels.test.ts

pitfalls.title: factor_research_temporal_semantics_and_release_evidence
symptoms: Feature, return-factor and benchmark series are treated as interchangeable.
Historical NAV rows are compressed or filled, or missing future prices determine the selected portfolio.
A research release is imported as already approved, or generic evidence bindings are described as automatic portfolio optimization.
An end-date-only study revision prevents comparable score-drift monitoring.
Overlapping forward-return labels are concatenated as factor returns, or rolling IC is dated as if future labels were known on the signal date.
ETF characteristic spreads are named SMB/HML, RF is silently zero-filled, or imported panels are advertised as verified official FF3/PIT data.
trigger_actions: edit factor calculations, attribution, study datasets or benchmark basis
change release monitoring or product-pool gateway dispatch
connect factor evidence to investment stages
check_before_edit: Keep performance benchmark, characteristic definitions and same-market/currency factor-return datasets separate; do not default US FF3 returns to China research.
Use active canonical real data, exact QDII metadata semantics (非QDII is domestic), stable SSE dates and announcement lag; current snapshots do not prove full historical revision PIT.
Purge training labels crossing the holdout boundary; never compress/fill missing NAV or preselect using future data availability; daily drift and both-sided turnover determine NAV costs.

Diagnostics must not mutate normalized factors, scores or labels: ascontiguousarray can alias a contiguous input. Pairwise IC filtering uses two owned asset-length work buffers reused across dates/factors; quantile assignments use unchanged signal-day scores even when future labels are missing. Version corrected results without rewriting prior run artifacts.
Check reference parity and actual NJIT dispatcher calls with fixed signatures, no Python fallback and startup readiness.
Run/release evidence is immutable; scheduled, expired, retired or stale releases cannot feed candidates; imports remain pending manual review.
Compare scoring context and factor snapshots for drift, allowing end date/revision changes; changed definitions, weights, universe or normalization are not comparable.
FACTOR_REAL_DATA=1 browser acceptance writes real research artifacts and candidates; keep it separate from offline fixtures and do not run it as an ordinary unit gate.
Separate per-signal cross-sectional IC from rolling IC statistics; use matured-label dates and keep holdout samples independent.
Characteristic spreads read checksum-verified frozen inputs, enter at the next trading close, and retain missing held-leg gaps instead of future-based reselection or survivor reweighting.

Custom FF3 2x3 construction requires explicit June/reference breakpoints, prior-year book equity announced before formation, December market cap, lagged daily market weights and complete daily RF; empty groups fail closed.
Generic total-return regressions have no risk-adjusted alpha claim. Check CSV status and content type before downloading; do not save JSON errors as data.

Fixed in-sample exposures are retrospective. Rolling windows preserve trading-day positions, exclude current/future returns and unannounced NAV, and invalidate failed refits rather than silently carrying stale successful coefficients.
Factor contributions reuse the same dated exposures; excess-return models restore RF for total-return reconciliation. Intercept and residual are separate components, not manager-skill claims.

Link interval contributions using beginning-of-day portfolio wealth; do not sum daily contributions or independently compound factor legs. A missing day invalidates full-interval attribution, and monthly summaries restart wealth independently.

Reconciliation is an accounting identity, not model validation: inspect held-out R2, residuals and coverage. Legacy artifacts without daily contribution arrays must not acquire fabricated historical results in the UI.
safe_observation_methods: npm run test --prefix frontend -- --run FactorResearchCenter.test.tsx App.test.tsx ProductDetail.test.tsx

pitfalls.title: routing_facts_need_runtime_grounding_before_claims
symptoms: A module is marked mixed because code was read but its runtime smoke was not run.
Future agents treat static route facts as proof that UI or external integration works.
trigger_actions: use Hermes routes for a task touching mixed modules
promote implementation facts after only reading documentation
edit frontend or data-ingestion behavior without running the listed smoke commands
check_before_edit: Read grounding.unsampled_paths for selected modules.
Run the module minimum_regression command before claiming runtime behavior.
Keep new facts in repo_map/task_routes/pitfalls, not AGENTS.md.

pitfalls.title: routing_files_are_machine_owned_contracts
symptoms: task_routes duplicates repo_map operational file lists.
routing-only changes accidentally include business code.
AGENTS.md is used as a dumping ground for project facts instead of protocol.

A read_before_edit path passes coverage/path validation but is absent from route_task context because read_before_edit is absent from operational_list_resolution.apply_to_fields and from the rendered first_read/then_check lists.
Stable source, test, config or documentation paths are exempted by allowed_untracked_globs, masking files missing from Git.
trigger_actions: edit AGENTS.md or docs routing JSON
prepare routing-only commit
change project-local AI Hermes scripts
check_before_edit: Keep routing facts in JSON owners.
Run evolve and validate after routing changes.
Use routing-only changed-file lists for routing-only work.
Put mandatory module reading in first_read_files and inspect the actual route_task context; path coverage alone does not prove an agent will receive the requirement.

Restrict allowed_untracked_globs to genuine local diagnostic/cache artifacts. Keep new stable references visible as reproducibility failures until they are included in an authorized Git submission scope.

pitfalls.title: backend_app_contains_legacy_inline_routes_and_includes_modular_routers
symptoms: A change is made only in services/strategy_routes.py or services/analytics_routes.py while backend/app.py still has older inline endpoints with the same paths.
Tests import service routers directly, but integrated uvicorn behavior also depends on backend/app.py include order and exception swallowing.
A route appears to work in a unit test but differs when served through the app shell.
trigger_actions: change any /api/strategy endpoint
change /api/fit-classes, /api/rolling-corr, or /api/efficient-frontier
change app.include_router handling or FastAPI app setup
check_before_edit: Search backend/app.py and services routers for the same path before changing endpoint behavior.
Prefer the modular router as the behavioral owner when tests import it directly, but verify app-level registration.
Run service-router tests and at least py_compile for backend/app.py.

pitfalls.title: rebalance_window_contract_is_shared_across_api_backtest_and_ui
symptoms: rollingN requests silently use too few samples or start before enough history exists.
Backtest markers no longer align with returned series dates.
Static strategy behavior changes when a model window is invalid.
trigger_actions: edit slice_fit_data
edit ensure_valid_rebalance_window
edit gen_rebalance_dates
edit compute-schedule-weights or backtest handling
change ClassAllocation window_mode/data_len payloads
check_before_edit: Preserve all mode as full history to the target date.
Preserve rollingN as the latest data_len trading rows with a minimum of two rows.
Keep first valid rebalance date aligned with markers and returned series.

Pass NAV, lineage and available_at as one request-owned result through fitting and allocation persistence. Never restore a process-global last-load getter; verify interleaved requests cannot advance another product's knowledge time.
Run the window, rebalance, backtest, and strategy API tests.

pitfalls.title: local_parquet_data_is_required_but_not_present_in_bootstrap_checkout
symptoms: Data-backed APIs return 400 or 404 when parquet files are absent.
A code change assumes data/ exists in every checkout.
Trading-calendar behavior changes because the SSE calendar parquet is unavailable or has different columns.
trigger_actions: change DATA_DIR behavior
change parquet column names
change ETF ingestion scripts
change strategy, analytics, or product APIs that read parquet data
check_before_edit: Use tmp parquet fixtures or monkeypatch DATA_DIR in tests; do not require network calls.
Keep documented schemas aligned with readers in backend/app.py, fit.py, and trading_calendar.py.
Do not add large or sensitive local data files as routing references unless they are intentionally tracked artifacts.

pitfalls.title: indicator_runtime_must_preserve_restricted_ast_and_scalar_output_contracts
symptoms: A parser or operator change admits attribute access, subscripting, keywords, imports, or other non-whitelisted AST nodes.
Generated operator metadata diverges from callable arity or input/output types.
A legacy scalar root or a named scalar-bundle leaf returns an unchecked array/tuple instead of a finite scalar, or bypasses node/depth limits; a bundle is silently treated as its first leaf.
trigger_actions: edit cal_indicators runtime
edit LaTeX executor
change the controlled operator registry
change expression validation, topology, or final result handling
check_before_edit: Keep runtime definitions in memory and treat generated DSL JSON as optional metadata only.
Run malicious/invalid AST, operator arity/type, DAG budget, finite scalar-leaf and shared-node failure-isolation tests. Preserve legacy single-root behavior and keep named output identities explicit.
Keep NetworkX optional and do not make execution topology depend on DOT export support.

C++ AOT adaptation must preserve N NAV versus N-1 interval returns, metric-scoped parameter slots, historical source versions and per-root failure isolation. Resolve source-contract defaults by DSL and reject mismatches before native compilation; recording unvalidated version strings in the fingerprint is not a compatibility check. Prepared run/run_audit borrows output; retained results require run_snapshot. Platform prepare must wrap all three run methods and validate each result audit before returning; validating only execute is insufficient. Every result must match the bound graph fingerprint and method-specific lifetime (execute/snapshot independent; prepared run/audit borrowed), and third-party C++ feature/postprocess stages require their own complete matching audits. Never fabricate NJIT signatures for native execution or infer that service warmup was removed.

pitfalls.title: frontend_pages_are_tightly_coupled_to_backend_payload_and_browser_rendering_contracts
symptoms: Frontend pages have many direct fetch calls whose payloads must match backend route models.
Vitest can cover state and API flows while ECharts, KaTeX, responsive layout, and keyboard focus still require browser acceptance.

A public production deployment exposes a write endpoint without an explicit enable decision.
Full-refresh files become visible before read-only validation and atomic manifest activation complete.
A successful Tushare fetch is repeated because local snapshot post-processing failed.
Late or revised observations are skipped because incremental overlap rows do not replace matching stored keys.
Incremental merge mixes string or integer stored dates with Timestamp values and Arrow conversion fails before schema alignment.
Independent worker limiters or worker-side Parquet writes exceed the account quota or expose partially merged data.

ETL API restart reconnects the detached executor by run/attempt/nonce and OS process birth. Close the launcher FD without LOCK_UN; a shared open-file-description unlock would also unlock the live child. Service restart must verify the recorded project, command, cwd, OS process birth and independent session before signalling its group. Source-center mutations require a loopback connection as well as Origin/Sec-Fetch validation; an absent or forged matching Origin is not authentication. Forwarded headers and an allowed-origin setting never grant a remote client write authority.

Cross-date ETL collection is a non-blocking recovery warning, separate from execution/lock/artifact blockers. Preserve attempt collection windows and migration origins; use batch receipts when present, label old execution windows as estimates, and never substitute collection time for available_at or certify PIT from same-day collection. Local-only resume must not imply another supplier download.

Current fund contract inception does not bound predecessor history: local 000264/000595 holdings predate their 2013/2014 contracts. Observed fund_portfolio start/end filter ann_date (000011.OF, 20150826-20210301, observed 2026-09-08), despite doc 121 saying report period. Partition by fund/announcement range and validate every announcement without silently filtering rows; preserve reports older than the range and both split halves. events_v4 freezes range_field=ann_date and isolates v3 receipts. Never discard history solely by found_date/type/liquidation. Checkpoint each leaf, confirm empties, cancel quota waits, and acknowledge caps only after replacement shards validate. Old empty markers are not proof; old nonempty day shards need a verified migration receipt.

Do not wrap exhausted typed transport errors into RuntimeError: the worker intentionally hides arbitrary exception text. Preserve safe source error codes and bounded attempt context, never raw credentials/URLs; disk, programming and contract errors are not retryable network failures. Cross-version holdings recovery must verify current events_v4 contract, every nonempty shard checksum/page/row/identity/PIT field and two-confirmation empty receipts before cloning. Keep source receipts and collection times immutable, revalidate copied evidence on resume, and never treat SPLIT as complete coverage or import v3 under v4.

A user-approved interface request-rate change still creates a new revision. Only the explicit migration accept-rate-change option may compare parsed default-equivalent configurations while excluding requests_per_minute and min_interval_seconds for the named interface; all other source/data semantics stay exact. Locate old shards by the old configuration hash and clone verified evidence under the new hash, recording both revisions/rates. Normal resume never ignores configuration differences. Local shared quotas do not cover other machines using the same account.

Stream a bounded, redacted log tail instead of capture_output, retain checkpoints after interruption, and expose persisted modules/scopes as a safe one-click retry contract when the supervising API process is lost.
Long local Parquet merges must emit flushed progress often enough to refresh the supervisor's activity timer; do not treat a silent CPU-bound merge as idle.
Write full refreshes to an isolated version, build the local metrics snapshot, validate it, and atomically switch the manifest; keep the old manifest on any failure.
Treat analytics rebuild or promotion failure as a warning after successful fetching so operators can rebuild locally without another Tushare call.
Refetch the configured trading-day overlap and let incoming rows replace matching keys while preserving atomic sorted output.
Normalize date values before deduplication, then serialize them back to the existing Parquet Arrow date-column type before conversion and atomic replacement.

Make every worker share the source/API quota and retry policy; keep pagination sequential within each date. Workers may atomically write their own disjoint request checkpoints, never the shared final output. Only the coordinator publishes the fully validated final Parquet.

Copy untouched instrument groups in Arrow, preserve the original Parquet when the merged content is identical, and reuse a non-stale analytics snapshot only when every analytics source fingerprint is unchanged.

Resolve inserted indicators by indicator_id plus revision on the server, require matching context and DSL/registry/data/schema versions, and expand to an independent scalar expression rather than a mutable runtime reference.

Runtime-constant series parameters require explicit parameter_contract_version 1.0 and author-opened positions. Preserve older frozen-default contracts; merge and validate defaults plus overrides per instance, recompute lookback and output ranges, include effective values in cache/export provenance, and reuse the prewarmed NJIT signature. Canvas parameter nodes must roundtrip without becoming data variables or literals.

When lifting a scalar indicator into a rolling series, lock the source revision and definition hash and execute the complete eligible scalar subgraph in each window. Preserve explicit runtime-parameter contracts; local sample/day/risk-free context belongs to that scope, never to the whole series.

Keep every existing anchor date even when its value is NaN/Inf. Derive returns on the uncompressed NAV axis, retain the leading unavailable return, and load a preceding observation only for bodies that require a level/date baseline. Verify displayed tails against the same dates from a full calculation.
Initial metadata/catalog responses must not overwrite edits made while loading. Only initialize untouched technical defaults; keep validation unavailable until the registry is loaded.

AI page evidence keeps editor, active preview and displayed requests separate. Freeze exact definitions, locked revisions, submitted overrides and requested/effective dates; never label old results with new controls. Model reads must use registered server projections, not raw page arrays or client scalar claims. Preserve last-result status and safe original-request references; current-request recomputation is not proof of an older displayed result. Withhold client fee values even in request views, and invalidate old page/context receipts and summaries without invalidating confirmed preferences. Save retries after a lost response must reuse the original confirmation and request ID, including after closing/reopening the panel. Host remounts lose in-memory attempts: deduplicate the full definition within the session using durable commit receipts, restore saved status from the server, and never let new confirmation/request IDs bypass an uncertain prior write. Restored successful saves must refresh the host catalog, sharing notification deduplication with direct success for the same session and full definition. Reconcile the card success feedback too; do not keep a resolved save error or suppress errors from subsequent actions. A nullable requested date resolves through the existing PIT policy; comparison and metric override dates remain separate. Cancellation on research-object unmount includes late accepted requests; ordinary panel closing does not cancel. Repeated reads compare selected section content, not random snapshot IDs. Task-state freshness also checks the receipt page-content stamp and the current valid draft hash; missing dependency stamps cannot certify current evidence. Keep stale receipts readable as history, but do not reselect cached task/plan/memory/context-read wrappers as fresh evidence. Scenario failures need their own state, preserved across unrelated page operations and cleared by a new scenario attempt. Fence catalog versions after tool execution and at every model response boundary, including compaction/finalization; discard stale output while preserving previously applied progress and actual model usage. Fence current-data tools before and after execution, including portfolio scenario recomputation; discard changed-generation results before model admission. Immutable portfolio diagnosis/evaluation still reads its frozen run and must not be cancelled solely by external market-data refresh. Block sends while restoring a stored session, including failed reads until reconnect; unresolved state is not a missing session. Message retries freeze their original resume parent, including absence, while refreshing the optimistic session revision. Replay must not cancel the accepted run; an accepted edited message can replay after restoration removed its original target. Hydrating memory fields from the first full session snapshot must trigger memory loading even at the same session revision. Terminal run updates are not complete session snapshots: reload proposals and memory sources once when a running turn ends through SSE or polling, even if session_revision is unchanged. Reuse recovery identity/version fencing, preserve unsent input, clear disconnection feedback after successful recovery, and keep memory decisions separate from business saves. After memory accept/reject/revoke, read the session proposal state before refreshing accepted records. Block memory mutations while reads are pending or failed; recovery reads state without resending a write, so a lost acceptance response cannot turn the same proposal into a replacement decision. Automatic indicator-definition memory proposals, accepted records and UI replacement matching must share the same scope-level object and full-definition key. Normalize old definition-hash identities only after validating original record signatures and provenance; preserve product-scoped preferences, explicit replacement versions and revocation. A stopped turn's queued message retains its send lock while the session read is pending until POST takes over. A cancelled queue ignores late reads; failed or skipped sends retain a retryable message, never an orphaned queued bubble.

Keep the headline formula semantic and compact: use symbols such as mu, sigma, s, windowed min/max, smoothing S, or drawdown D; keep min_periods, NaN branches and implementation recurrences in the detailed DAG explanation.
Respect ann_date <= as_of for reported NAV fields and surface partial coverage instead of silently filling or claiming full availability.

Require revision for every mutable update/delete and run plans against independent indicator IDs and locked revisions, never removed scalar child-result references. When save/readback changes draft source or metadata, invalidate old inline compile tokens before preview/export; equivalent LaTeX is not the same exact token payload.

Merge scalar computation nodes only under identical bindings, operator versions and input/window contracts. Preparation locks revisions before evaluation; formal evaluation must not compile a missing plan or rerun independent formulas as a fallback.

Snapshot scalars and dates use independent locked definitions. Time-series snapshots require channel_id plus last_finite and use the full requested window before display truncation; preserve the selected value date, channel format and missing status. Never use warmup values or the last 5000 chart points as the snapshot calculation source.
Exclude products missing any selected metric from ranking instead of treating missing values as zero.

Agent state restoration must respect ownership: persisted human memory decisions and business commit receipts outlive a turn snapshot. Reconcile proposal status from decision receipts on reads and writes, retain independently decided/manual proposals across edits, and replay decisions even after proposal pruning. A source quote identifies the user evidence, not the run that created a proposal or plan; legacy edits without base snapshots must use applied receipt ownership and preserve earlier reused IDs. Superseded tool receipts remain auditable but cannot return through context.read. Test stop/decision/edit ordering, repeated edits, old persisted inconsistency, replacement/revocation and absent proposals. Frontend control successes and failures must belong to the mounted session/run; late errors after a terminal transition or a newer run must not overwrite current feedback, while closing a panel does not invalidate its live request. Internal artifact ownership must use stable IDs and validated arguments, never depend on an identifier surviving the bounded model projection. If a session restore already confirms the pending message, a late POST response must preserve its newer run state and session fields; a late transport failure must not roll back accepted text or offer another write.

Keep recovery completion boundaries explicit. An in-flight message owns its pending context; switch the accepted run and its frozen context together, including ordinary send, edit, queue and retry when an older session GET returns first. A matching restored receipt remains authoritative and genuine later page changes still invalidate. A finished tool thread is not proof that quarantine release persisted: retry a durable terminal-run fence through the existing reconciliation entry only after its local owner, runner completion and absence of live tool threads are verified. Transient storage errors must not leave an irrecoverable busy session or permit overlapping execution. Cover restoration before and after POST acceptance, changed and unchanged page contexts, and failed cleanup followed by storage recovery; preserve prior progress and failure reasons without rerunning tools. Preview-based context adoption must prove the preview belongs to the current run; a retained older preview cannot authorize a new run even when the page returns to its old conditions. Keep controller initialization, request acceptance/task registration and reconciliation on the same event-loop thread across every HTTP entry, including preview reads; offload only the blocking artifact read. Test accepted-but-not-yet-registered runs against concurrent historical preview requests, and verify slow preview I/O does not block run control.

Enforce state ownership at write boundaries, not only individual callers. Frontend POST, full snapshots, SSE phases, polling and control replies share run admission: only authoritative receipts can switch run plus frozen context; same-run versions and stopping/terminal state cannot regress. Hydrate same-revision session memory without restoring an older run fence. Only a failed session GET with 404 clears the session; subordinate event/run failures preserve it for reconnect. Controllers reject the wrong thread or event loop before storage access; tool callbacks return to the owner loop, and shutdown fallback only retires finished local resources. Durable checkpoints require the current session run and owner epoch, reject terminal rewrites and active-to-queued regression, and do not append rejected artifacts/events/progress. Consume failed durable admission before starting every model or tool operation, including cancellation from another store/process; rejection must prevent dispatch while already-running operations retain their wait/quarantine cleanup. Publish tool-timeout failure and its error/reply together through finalization; do not mark terminal before the reply is committed. Recovery revalidates its observed run revision and epoch inside the transaction, never clears another run operation, preserves terminal results during cleanup, and advances run revision on quarantine release. Check legal cancellation/finalization, human decisions, completed worker recovery and both callback return orders alongside rejection cases. Apply the same durable gate to successful and exceptional model returns before primary replies, compaction or finalization can consume them. Return admission is not a committed body: cancellation or error finalization must rebuild from the last durable checkpoint, never resurrect a tool result whose completion write failed. Read cancellation, build the control reply and publish the terminal state in one existing SQLite transaction; checkpoint must reuse that transaction and rollback with it. Test both cancellation/terminal commit orders, remote cancellation during model work, temporary completion-write failure, normal next-turn and explicit resume history, actual usage, and preservation of prior committed progress. Separate execution admission from content checkpoints: control events persist only bounded execution metadata, never candidate conversations, detector state or tool traces. Rejected content commits cannot publish model messages or compaction events, even if a caller ignores the boolean. Normal finish also starts from durable content and accepts only an explicit final reply; interrupt cannot publish tentative work. Commit context only after compaction installs its candidate. Bind a discarded tool notice to its latest committed plan, not the first reused call_id in history. Keep frontend session metadata and run/frozen/adopted context in one published core; derive duplicated run fields and treat phase updates as phase-only, never a replay of response artifacts.

Persist the operation fence together with started admission before dispatch. Timeout, cancellation, shutdown or a later control-write failure cannot release a still-running tool; completed receipts and the single real-future completion callback release only their matching operation. Retry failed durable cleanup through reconciliation, preserve owner/capacity until real exit, and observe late exceptions on every exit path. Keep ordinary active-operation protection internal; terminal quarantine remains public. Pair provider call IDs within the preceding assistant batch, never globally across the transcript. Share that sequence rule across model admission, checkpoint scrubbing, compaction projection and pending-call closure. Allow reuse after a completed batch; reject duplicate/orphan/incomplete batches and future-name borrowing. Unknown or malformed legacy history must remain safely omitted or blocked without making terminal error publication fail again. Test real thread overlap, failed writes, both callback orders, legal multi-batch reuse, signatures, and malformed-history finalization.

Keep one execution authority per fact: derive pending calls from the final committed assistant batch minus its tool results; never dispatch or block compaction from a separate pending_calls cache. Resume only unchanged, sanitized pending plans; historical closed calls remain closed across every checkpoint interruption. Store-owned lifecycle transitions must not copy a caller status: start once from queued, cancel to stopping, and use the terminal/recovery methods. A completed or unknown receipt must match the original started operation, tool and arguments; blocked/not_executed cannot overwrite dispatched or closed calls. Preserve physical execution phase separately when a receipt is discarded, so callback cleanup order cannot change completion admission. Test both allowed continuations and rejected writes, including real partial-batch shutdown/resume.

Treat null and omitted operator parameter bounds as unbounded, not zero. Preserve explicit zero/lower/upper bounds and validate real JSON metadata in formula-builder round-trip tests; derive fixed-window browser fixtures explicitly instead of relying on a renamed parameterized built-in.

Bind commit-preview revision and full definition hash to the durable current draft; freeze the stored definition and recheck its identity before a new business commit, including confirmations written by older code. New resumes may reference only the latest session run; reject older pending batches before acceptance while preserving idempotent replay of already accepted messages and completed saves. Compare every definition field with JSON numeric round-trip equivalence only (0 and 0.0); boolean/string aliases remain distinct, and preserve the stored definition hash rather than changing global receipt hashing.

AI business services are explicitly mounted on the request application; never recover missing bindings by importing HTTP routers, scanning sys.modules or creating another service. Product HTTP adapters and agent callbacks use the same instrument_service implementation. Tool declarations own current-data policies: immutable portfolio evaluation/diagnosis must stay separate from scenario recomputation. Keep indicator preview loading and same-run adoption in the indicator adapter; the shared conversation owns identity/version/cancellation and only transports existing artifact DTOs. Keep SQLite run transitions atomic when separating domain code. Metadata must reject a missing application service with 503 before the best-effort catalog catch; configured LLM settings alone do not prove the agent service is mounted.

A save button cannot pre-authorize an unseen commit-preview impact. Persist the server preview, show its frozen definition/context and same-name creation warning, then require a separate human confirmation before commit. Cancellation performs no business write; retries of an already confirmed uncertain request retain its confirmation and idempotency key. Test both cancellation and acceptance, localized/multi-channel previews and response-loss recovery. Commit-preview itself increments session_revision. Admit that authoritative receipt through the shared conversation input before asking for confirmation, even if the user cancels or a later commit fails. Advance only the matching session version, preserve run/context/memory ownership, reject stale or foreign receipts, and test cancellation followed by another message against a version-enforcing fixture. Apply the same version-only admission to successful commit receipts before refreshing the full snapshot; a failed follow-up read must not erase the acknowledged save version. Memory accept/reject/replace/revoke receipts, including idempotent replay, return the current session ID and version from their transaction and use the same frontend receipt admission. Keep decision/snapshot errors separate from list-read errors so a late successful list read cannot unlock unresolved memory actions. Audit all session-mutating HTTP paths when changing this protocol.

Scenario AI drafts must use the regime_graph domain and registered scalar parameter contracts; inline observations, qualification receipts and business identity cannot enter authored DTOs. Applying revalidates the merged graph, fences late responses with editor context identity, preserves editor-owned references, and invalidates old qualifications. Hidden retained workbenches must not mount portal assistants. Verify test_agent_regimes.py and RegimeAgentPanel.test.tsx.

Scenario library questions must search saved definitions separately from built-in templates. Read by explicit ID and revision through the mounted graph service, retain duplicate-name choices and pagination, and project only registered scalar settings and graph structure. An empty editor snapshot is not an empty saved library; definition access does not certify PIT availability or trigger calculation. Verify saved-library HTTP model-admission tests in test_agent_regimes.py.

Indicator write requests must reach metrics.validate and a saveable draft before the existing human-confirmed commit. task.read/task.plan are optional task records, not write prerequisites. Keep strict case-sensitive argument schemas; on validation failure or blocked repeated calls, return registry-owned field guidance without exception text, unknown keys or input values. Do not ask users for an existing write API or treat argument errors as missing permissions. Verify capitalized task.read recovery, draft delivery, confirmation and idempotent saves in test_agent_api.py.

Central intent proposals are not business completion or write authorization. Ground routes in shared platform navigation and registered actions. Accept only a current completed source run; create the target session, first run and handoff receipt in one transaction, and schedule after commit. Replays restore the target session latest context, never the initial handoff conditions. Frontend cancellation ownership starts before dispatch and transfers only after session admission. Cancel an unresolved handoff by its known source session/run/intent, even when its POST response is lost. Serialize cancellation with acceptance in the existing source transaction: cancel the immutable accepted run or persist a fence rejecting later acceptance. Repeat cancellation must not affect a subsequent run. Use router navigation for application-owned return and LLM settings links so component cleanup runs. Receipt validation and failed-promise cleanup remain request-owned; readiness changes or StrictMode must not drop or reacquire cancellation ownership. Test both acceptance/cancellation orders, real HTTP terminal state, lost responses and the actual return link in a browser. Admit restoration snapshots by session/page identity and version even when the panel is closed or observation is disabled; stale snapshots must not overwrite a newer run, and newer snapshots must not be dropped solely because the observer stopped. Restore conditions from the actual selected session, including a locally stored replacement after clearing; never combine an old handoff context with a new session. Freeze the handoff request and context baseline before its first dispatch, and retain both across effect replays and response-loss retries. Preserve explicit empty references and edits throughout handoff and restoration waits; cover receipt/read/unmount orders, retry after edits and refresh after replacement. Generate cancellation request IDs only in the shared frontend service from the immutable run or handoff intent ID; do not concatenate session and run IDs beyond the backend 64-character bound. Use production-length IDs and verify the actual HTTP route reaches cancelled, not just that a mocked request was observed. Keep offline contract checks separate from explicit live-model intent evaluation.

CopilotKit is a transport adapter to the existing Python run authority, not a second executor. Do not dispatch tools or trust history, identity, approval, drafts or model settings from AG-UI messages/state. Reuse server page-instance/scope/domain/PIT/admission/version gates. Keep runId stable across transport retries and distinguish it from the backend run_id; exact cancellation must persist before acceptance and must not stop a newer request. Physical tool quarantine outlives transport cancellation; disconnect only detaches observation. Confirm crash recovery with a killed independent process and a durable checkpoint, not just restored chat history. Keep save and memory decisions on their original human-confirmed APIs. Reconnect after independent writes to update session revisions. Request-scoped Authorization/Cookie/PIT headers cannot be cached globally or selected by forwardedProps. Register browser proxies through copilotkit/client.mjs before rendering chat. The pinned CopilotKit client drops activeRun on connect; its default stop then omits runId. Bind cancellation to the observed RUN_STARTED thread/run pair, preserve that pair across disconnects, isolate clones and ignore obsolete observation callbacks. New sends keep the SDK-owned input runId, including before their first server receipt. Test actual CopilotKitCore.stopAgent after connect and delayed old stops reaching a newer backend run; direct ResearchRunner.stop tests alone miss this path.

symptoms: The same raw indicator value is rendered with different scaling, precision, or unit across detail, comparison, evaluation, and portfolio pages.
A frontend infers percent or currency formatting from an indicator name instead of MetricPresentation.
A missing, insufficient, failed, or inapplicable result is displayed as zero or loses its stable reason code.
A historical evaluation result is formatted by looking up the latest catalog revision rather than using the locked presentation embedded in the result.
A selector hides an indicator only from a static ETF/fund label, or shows it without explaining which selected products lack the required fields.
localStorage persists products, results, or historical as-of values instead of only indicator IDs and the runtime period.
trigger_actions: edit MetricPresentation construction or evaluate result payloads
edit shared metric selectors, value/status components, or browser preferences
edit product research, detail, comparison, evaluation-plan, dashboard, or portfolio metric displays
blast_radius: cross-page indicator selection and browser defaults
check_before_edit: Embed the locked MetricPresentation in every evaluation result and use it directly in frontend rendering.
Keep value_scale, display_format, precision, unit, notation, direction, version, and applicability explicit; never infer them from display names.
Render null as an explicit unavailable state with warnings and never coerce it to zero or include it in ranking.

Filter selectors by calculation context, keep field-dependent indicators visible, and use per-product input requirements to explain full or partial runtime availability while preserving hidden compatibility definitions for historical locked runs.

Keep browser display preferences limited to valid indicator/output selections and runtime periods; never persist raw results. Named scalar leaves retain their locked units, neutral direction and individual windows.

pitfalls.title: indicator_batch_workers_require_generation_bound_arrays_and_single_owner_cleanup
symptoms: One evaluation plan rereads the same Parquet source for each metric or period.
Worker tasks serialize NumPy payloads instead of passing shared-memory or mmap descriptors and integer window bounds.
A data refresh reuses cached arrays or windows from an older snapshot generation.
Multiple Uvicorn workers each create a process pool, or BLAS and Numba threads multiply process-level concurrency.
Timeout, cancellation, worker failure, or service restart leaves shared arrays or mmap files behind.
A request performs first-use Numba compilation instead of using lifespan-prewarmed fixed signatures.
A snapshot shortcut removes only part of a saved evaluation-plan fused batch, creating an unsaved subset shape that misses the startup-warmed immutable batch plan.
Large paged results outlive their bounded TTL or return an unstable missing/expired contract.
trigger_actions: edit indicator batch loading, window caching, fused kernels, process scheduling, or scoring
edit shared-memory, mmap, worker lifespan, timeout, or admission logic
edit evaluation-plan result pagination, retention, or execution metadata
change Docker worker, shm, BLAS, Numba, or indicator cache configuration
blast_radius: API process availability and CPU saturation
temporary shared resources and paged result retention
check_before_edit: Resolve locked formulas and physical dependencies once, scan each required Parquet source once, and key data/window/result caches by active data generation.
Pass only shared-memory or mmap descriptors and numeric plans to workers; keep strings and presentation assembly in the API process.
Use one Uvicorn worker per container, prewarm fixed Numba signatures in lifespan workers, and cap BLAS, process, and Numba concurrency with CPU tokens.

Preserve saved fused-batch membership at runtime: snapshot reuse may skip a fused group only when the whole group and all targets are covered; partial snapshot hits must execute the original warmed batch instead of constructing a new subset shape.
Keep parent ownership of unlink, terminate failed workers before shared cleanup, and remove only protected orphan resources whose owner PID is gone.
Keep result-cache TTL, 410 RESULT_EXPIRED, page bounds, and Retry-After busy responses stable.

pitfalls.title: frontier_controls_preserve_sampling_precision_and_grid_domains
symptoms: Risk selection no longer changes later random walks.
Constraint repair destroys the selected weight step.
Grid adoption uses continuous weights despite a configured discrete step.
trigger_actions: edit frontier generation, controls, constraints, metrics or weight adoption
check_before_edit: Keep all first-round seeds; later rounds select minimum risk per return bucket and freeze parent seeds for the next round.
All adopted weights must satisfy the selected integer step, total budget, single and overlapping group limits together.
Keep continuous grid coordinates as evidence; quantized adoption uses separately recomputed integer-feasible weights and metrics.
Keep target count independent from local refinement and per-target iterations; keep effective controls in one frontier workspace.
Return EWM window must affect sampling, refinement, grid solving and adoption under the same metric contract.

pitfalls.title: funding_capital_replay_and_saa_clock_consistency
symptoms: Reported capital meets the adoption probability but the displayed amount fails when replayed.
A cutoff change leaves an old SAA preview adoptable.
trigger_actions: edit investment goal numerical diagnosis
edit SAA preview, adoption or research clock handling
check_before_edit: Replay the displayed cent-rounded gate capital on the original draws and original payment/terminal success conditions; derive every reported probability from the actual count. Inverse capital rankings alone do not prove the floating-point gate.
Keep the saved funding simulation seed and path count separate from SAA candidate-search settings.
Invalidate unsaved policy previews and late responses on cutoff changes, guard adoption, and preserve already saved historical snapshots.

Treat an undefined research day as unknown and block goal/CMA/policy calculations and writes; null is only an explicitly confirmed no-cutoff view. Transitions between these states invalidate unsaved results and late replies.
Only preview/confirm may create mandate versions; unconfirmed historical inputs remain readable but cannot drive a new policy. Input-only confirmations still freeze their simulation settings.
Return from TAA with the selected baseline ID and read its immutable server snapshot. Do not replace adopted policy evidence with an allocation-only browser draft.

Mandate 2.0 risk levels resolve to upper caps, never minimum volatility constraints. Pending reference research may be saved but cannot silently acquire a numeric authorization. Keep original request inputs separate from resolved immutable constraints.

Separate reference search from fixed-candidate validation. A capital diagnostic after failed search is not a validated recommendation and must not authorize risk. Actual SAA adoption uses its own independent check; finite candidate failure is not an infeasibility proof.

A shared cash budget is independent of the three objective kinds. Cash protection requires the effective cash-role floor in SAA and the frozen TAA gate, not merely tradable liquid assets. Missing frozen cash evidence must fail closed.

Adding study parameters can make shared draft-shape validation discard supported earlier drafts. Adapt missing study fields at the mandate boundary without loosening the global draft guard or changing original inputs.

Funding-suggestion mode requires a cash budget and an explicit funding_target or cash_protection. Withdrawal rows alone must not bypass probability validation and produce a validated recommendation; manual/numeric budget-only research retains its separate semantics.

PIT initialization and clock changes invalidate editable mandate drafts only. A saved view must retain its frozen request, assessment and readonly state even when the clock resolves after the version; never turn it into a new active mandate.
Cloning compact non-funding mandates must preserve explicit cash_protection and terminal-floor amount basis with the cash budget; otherwise probability validation silently disappears.

New SAA previews require an active mandate. Publishing rechecks activity under the same governance lock used for retirement/replacement; historical mandate and baseline reads remain immutable and available.

Risk Scale retirement is mutable governance: frozen policy numbers remain readable, but current TAA/product application must recheck the exact scale hash and eligibility from the real workspace. Missing context or unavailable governance fails closed; saved eligibility is not current permission.

pitfalls.title: implementation_cash_and_candidate_evidence
symptoms: Class weights match but residual or total active risk exceeds the mandate.
Later cash replenishment hides a historical missed payment.
Changed inputs are finalized with a previous validation report.
trigger_actions: edit product risk, cost, continuation or package finalization
check_before_edit: Keep Q funding budgets separate from joint beta and full residual covariance. D=0 and zero active alpha are explicit forward assumptions. A originals are diagnostic; B originals all gate.

Charge each buy/sell side against post-cost holdings through the common self-financing solve. Unknown rates or settlement dates are unavailable; NAV does not fund cash payments. Already-paid costs require already-target holdings.
Use original monthly cashflow occurrence identities and inflation base; remaining 1/13/37 and zero months preserve terminal and missed-payment semantics. Original reserve is not deducted twice.

Copy provenance points to a validated immutable package artifact ID, not the logical package ID; updates preserve the stored copied_from_id even when the client omits or replaces it. A report belongs to the exact candidate and revision. Lock the candidate before validation and recheck source governance, data/code/fee fingerprints before finalization. Immutable reports remain readable when current use expires. Artifact admission checks the final UTF-8 manifest byte size including metadata against the same limit as reads, before promotion and index registration; oversized failures must leave existing package lists and history readable.

Reserve the shared compute slot before freezing a candidate. Busy validation must leave revisions and attempts unchanged so the same revision/key can retry; release the slot even if freezing fails. A frozen-candidate validation is distinct from independent simulation. Only a completed simulation on the validation random stream can assert independent_simulation. Local named research finalization is not authenticated independent review.
